newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian gold production up 3 pct in Q1 - report.
newsitem.headline: Australian gold production up 3 pct in Q1 - report.

text.p: Australian gold production for the first quarter of 1997 was 72.5 tonnes, or 2.3 million ounces, up three percent on the year-earlier period, mining consultant Surbiton Associates Pty Ltd said on Sunday.

Surbiton said the quarterly output figure was an excellent result given adverse factors such as the weather and followed record production of 292 tonnes for the 1996 year and 75.7 tonnes for the December 1996 quarter.
It said its Australian gold quarterly review identifies 99 percent of all new gold mined in Australia.

Western Australia produced 80 percent of all primary gold for the quarter, but was affected by high rainfall in the northern half of the state, with some areas reporting the highest rainfall on record, Surbiton said.
The Super Pit at Kalgoorlie, owned equally by Homestake Gold of Australia and Normandy Mining Ltd, retained its position as the largest Australian gold-producing operation.
March quarter production of 180,814 ounces was similar to the December quarter figure.

Surbiton said the star performer was Granny Smith, owned 60 percent by Placer Dome Inc's Pacific Pacific and 40 percent by Delta Gold NL. Production rose by 112 percent to 120,992 ounces, making it the second-largest producer.
Granny Smith also achieved the lowest cash cost for the quarter at A$202 per ounce.

Worst affected by the adverse weather was Newcrest Mining Ltd's Telfer operation, which produced 29 percent less gold than the previous quarter, with a 40 percent increase in cash costs, despite a 10 percent increase in grade.
Record rainfall of over a third of a meter (one yard) resulted in closure of the mine access road for five weeks during the quarter.
The weighted average cash cost for operations representing 82 percent of all primary production was A$376 per ounce.
